title: Compact credential handoff, resilient stream reconnect, and ergonomic SDK surface polish
author: Asha Menon
description: Context and motivation: Several customers and internal integrations reported edgecases where long-running streaming consumers hit transient auth failures during credential rotation and then observed poor reconnect ergonomics (double-retry storms, confusing error surfaces in the SDKs, and inconsistent behavior across Python/TS/Go). This PR implements a compact credential handoff protocol and stream reconnect stabilization heuristics, plus small ergonomic surface changes across the three SDKs to align behavior and reduce footguns. Goals: 1) make credential switch atomic and observable for streaming consumers, 2) avoid reconnect thundering through jittered backoff and bounded fast-retries, 3) provide a small, backwards-compatible API polish that reduces boilerplate when swapping credential providers. Summary of changes: - Introduce a CompactCredHandoff abstraction (language-native adapters in py/ts/go) that encodes an idempotent handoff token, prefetch window, and optional preemptive-reauth hint. The runtime uses the token to perform a single atomic swap without forcing stream restart for compatible server-side routing. - Streaming reconnects: add adaptive reconnect policy with capped aggressive retries (3 fast attempts within 8s) then switch to exponential backoff with randomized jitter and a long-term heartbeat to detect silent stream closures. - SDK ergonomic polish: add SDK helper constructors (fromCredentialChain, fromProviderWithWarmup) and a shorthand stream.consume_iterable API in Python/TS for common patterns; Go SDK gets a small helper that returns a typed channel with cancel semantics. - Telemetry and observability: emit cred_handoff.{attempt,result,latency}, stream.reconnect.{attempt,mode}, and stream.termination.{reason} metrics and attach cred_handoff_id to trace/span metadata when available. - Compatibility and versioning: bump Python SDK v0.21.0, TS SDK v1.8.0, Go SDK v0.9.4. Changes are implemented in a feature-flag guarded rollout (sdk.flags:compact_cred_handoff default off for 48h in canary, then on). Migration notes: existing credential providers keep working; providers that opt in to the new CompactCredHandoff adapter get lock-free handoffs and fewer transient disconnects. Design rationale: atomic handoff token minimizes window where two tokens are live and avoids duplicated reexpires; bounded fast-retries address hot start scenarios without causing platform overload; small API helpers reduce repetitive boilerplate across users and align behavior between SDKs. Backwards compatibility: no breaking surface changes to existing constructor signatures; new helpers are additive. Testing strategy: unit tests for adapter behavior in all SDKs, integration tests with local stream simulator (inject auth failure mid-stream), and e2e smoke run against dedicated canary deployment. Related: ENG-914 implements server-side handoff routing; ENG-921 is the rollout plan and dashboards.

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Nice clear interface. Two quick asks: add an explicit timeout on the handoff exchange and document the semantics when the server does not support atomic handoff.
Asha Menon: Added handoff_timeout param (default 5s) and documented fallback behavior (SDK falls back to graceful restart) in docs/compact-cred-handoff.md, pushed commit e8b9c72.
Sara Patel: Can we avoid adding global flags for now? Prefer scoping to SDK client config so we don't leak experiments into unrelated consumers.
Asha Menon: Agreed. Reworked the feature flag to be client-scoped (ClientConfig.flags.compactCredHandoff) and updated tests accordingly (commit f0c1d55).
Yuki Nakamura: Go helper looks idiomatic but add a note about goroutine lifecycle when consumer forgets to cancel. Otherwise LGTM.
Asha Menon: Added example and comment in warmup_provider_example.go and added a small guard in the helper to return a cancel func that closes the channel to avoid leaks.
CI bot: e2e-canary failed on first run (timeout on stream smoke test).
Asha Menon: Investigated — cause was test flakiness due to a race in the local simulator; added deterministic scheduling and retried. CI passed on rerun.
merge_details: Merged via squash by Sara Patel. Commit message condensed to: 'compact cred handoff + adaptive stream reconnect + sdk ergonomic helpers; bump versions'. Merged to main and backported to release/2026-02 for immediate TS/Go quickfixes.
release_notes: Add CompactCredHandoff adapter and adaptive stream reconnect policy. SDK helpers for credential warmup and simplified stream consumption added to Python/TypeScript/Go. Improved telemetry for handoff/reconnect events. Bumped SDK versions: Python v0.21.0, TypeScript v1.8.0, Go v0.9.4.
